microsoft-azure-consumption-commitment.title: Azure Consumption Commitment benefit – Microsoft Marketplace – Microsoft Learn
microsoft-azure-consumption-commitment.notes: A Microsoft Azure Consumption Commitment is a contractual agreement in which an organization promises to spend a defined amount on Azure over an agreed period. Under the Azure Consumption Commitment benefit, eligible purchases made through Microsoft Marketplace count automatically toward that commitment. Offers that carry the "Azure benefit eligible" badge qualify, and Azure services billed through a marketplace deployment under the Microsoft Product Terms generally count as well. For eligible offers from Microsoft partners, the full net purchase price before taxes is credited. To benefit, the organization needs a commitment agreement and an Azure subscription linked to it, and the buyer must sign in with a tenant tied to that organization. Buyers are advised to purchase in the Azure portal and use the "Get it in Azure portal" button at checkout. Limits apply: purchases funded by Azure prepayment, direct credit-card purchases in the marketplace and licenses used in hybrid or on-premises setups do not count, and agreements signed before the benefit existed may carry exclusions that the Microsoft account executive clarifies.

microsoft-certified-trainer.title: Microsoft Certified Trainer program – Microsoft Learn
microsoft-certified-trainer.notes: Microsoft Certified Trainer is an annual membership status for professionals who teach Microsoft technologies to customers. Microsoft Training Services Partners are required to have official Microsoft courseware delivered by MCTs, so the membership qualifies people to deliver that content. Members receive benefits such as software licenses, service credits and exam discounts, whose use follows the MCT Program Agreement and Microsoft licensing policies. A closed community called the MCT Lounge on the Microsoft Tech Community offers program meetings, courseware updates, discussion forums and feedback channels to Microsoft teams, and virtual or in-person events connect trainers with Microsoft staff and partners that post job offers. To join, applicants submit an online application and accept the MCT Program Agreement every year, and approved members must join the MCT Lounge. A separate Alumni program exists for trainers in good standing who no longer teach actively; it has no annual fee and keeps only lounge access and exam discounts. Specific eligibility criteria and benefit amounts are not detailed on the page itself.

microsoft-defender-easm.title: Defender External Attack Surface Management overview – Microsoft Learn
microsoft-defender-easm.notes: Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management continuously discovers and maps an organization's digital attack surface and gives an outside-in view of its online infrastructure. Security and IT teams use it to find unknown assets, prioritize risks and gain control over exposures beyond the firewall. Discovery relies on proprietary Microsoft technology that recursively follows observed connections from known legitimate assets, called discovery seeds, and infers which resources belong to the organization. Asset types include domains, IP blocks, hosts, email contacts, autonomous system numbers and Whois organizations. Found assets are indexed in an inventory and classified as recent or historic, and dashboards present insights on vulnerabilities, compliance and security hygiene. The inventory can be filtered, for example for assets linked to expiring infrastructure or for new cloud resources. Owner and Contributor roles can create, edit and delete resources and assets, while Reader can only view. Cross-tenant access, including through Azure Lighthouse, is not supported, and because discovery is based on inference it is not a full guarantee of coverage. After a resource is deleted, Microsoft cannot restore it.

microsoft-graph-schema-extensions.title: schemaExtension resource type – Microsoft Graph – Microsoft Learn
microsoft-graph-schema-extensions.notes: A schema extension in Microsoft Graph defines a schema that lets an app add strongly typed custom data to a resource type. The custom data appears as a complex type on the extended resource and is managed through the same REST request as the resource itself. Supported resources include user, group, administrativeUnit, contact, device, event, message, organization and post. The definition has an id, an owner (the appId of the owning application), a status, a list of typed properties, the target types it may be applied to and a description. The id can use a verified domain name plus schema name, or an ext prefix with eight alphanumeric characters. A definition starts as InDevelopment, where only the owner can update it additively or delete it. Once set to Available, it can be used by apps in all tenants, changes stay additive and deletion is no longer possible. In the Deprecated state the definition can no longer be read or changed, although stored values can still be read, updated and deleted. Available definitions are visible to every developer, but the data created from them is tenant specific and requires explicitly granted permissions. The id and owner cannot be changed after creation.

microsoft-purview-content-search.title: Content search in Microsoft Purview – Microsoft Learn
microsoft-purview-content-search.notes: Content search is a tool in the Microsoft Purview portal for quickly finding content across Microsoft 365. It can search email in Exchange mailboxes, documents on SharePoint sites and OneDrive locations, and chat messages, including content in Microsoft Teams and Microsoft 365 Groups. A search is created by choosing content sources and optionally entering a keyword query; without a query, all items in the chosen locations are returned. Conditions narrow the query, and keyword statistics help refine it. Search permissions filters can limit eDiscovery managers to a subset of mailboxes or sites. The tool can also cover cloud mailboxes of users with on-premises mailboxes, imported third-party data and Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts and responses stored in custodian mailboxes. Results can be exported, and messages can be deleted from mailboxes, for instance after a phishing attack. PowerShell scripts support targeted collections and bulk searches. Estimated and exported result counts can differ, and partially indexed items can be included or left out of an export. The page states that classic eDiscovery experiences were retired on 31 August 2025, so its guidance applies only to organizations hosted by 21Vianet in China; others should use the new eDiscovery experience.

microsoft-sentinel-data-lake.title: Microsoft Sentinel data lake overview – Microsoft Learn
microsoft-sentinel-data-lake.notes: Microsoft Sentinel data lake is a cloud-native, fully managed platform built to ingest, store and analyze large volumes of varied security data without provisioning or maintaining data infrastructure. Data is kept in the open Parquet format, so teams do not have to trade coverage against cost, and security data and telemetry can be retained for up to 12 years. The design uses two tiers. The analytics tier is the existing Sentinel data layer for advanced hunting, alerting and incident management. The data lake tier provides long-term central storage for queries and Python-based analysis, with data from the analytics tier mirrored into it. Analysts can run KQL queries in an editor with IntelliSense, schedule jobs that promote results from the lake to the analytics tier, and use Jupyter notebooks for machine learning, visualization and scheduled runs. Activity auditing is enabled by default and records KQL access, notebook runs and job changes. All existing Sentinel data connectors are supported as sources, covering Microsoft Defender, Microsoft 365, Entra ID, firewall and network logs, and third-party identity logs. Typical uses are forensics, incident response and anomaly detection on historical data. The page does not name license requirements or prices.

minimal-apis.title: Minimal APIs overview – ASP.NET Core – Microsoft Learn
minimal-apis.notes: Minimal APIs are described as the recommended way to build fast HTTP APIs with ASP.NET Core. They let developers create complete REST endpoints with little code and configuration by declaring routes and actions fluently, which avoids traditional scaffolding and unnecessary controllers. Endpoints are registered with methods such as MapGet on the application object, and route values are bound to lambda parameters. The page lists simpler syntax, less boilerplate, lower overhead compared with controllers, easier testing and a modern approach as reasons to choose them for new projects, though it gives no benchmarks. The approach can be configured and customized to scale to several APIs, complex routes, authorization rules and control over response content. The page also names features that controller-based APIs offer out of the box but that Minimal APIs lack or need custom solutions for: extensible model binding through IModelBinderProvider and IModelBinder, advanced validation through IModelValidator, application parts or the application model, and OData support. Tutorials and a quick reference are linked for further guidance.

mlops.title: MLOps: Model management, deployment, and monitoring with Azure Machine Learning – Microsoft Learn
mlops.notes: MLOps applies DevOps principles such as continuous integration, continuous delivery and continuous deployment to the lifecycle of machine learning models. Its aims are better quality and consistency of ML solutions, faster experimentation and model development, quicker deployment to production and stronger quality assurance with end-to-end lineage tracking. In Azure Machine Learning, reproducible pipelines chain steps like data preparation, feature extraction, hyperparameter tuning and evaluation, and reusable environments track pip and conda dependencies. Models are registered and versioned in a registry, identified by name and version. For production, a model is packaged as a Docker image and deployed to batch endpoints or online endpoints, with targets including managed online endpoints and Azure Kubernetes Service. Online endpoints support controlled rollout with several deployment versions, A/B testing and percentage-based traffic splitting. Job history, data asset tracking and interpretability support governance, while Azure Event Grid receives events such as run completion, model registration, deployment and data drift. Azure Pipelines can automate training and deployment. A registered model used in an active deployment cannot be deleted.

model-router.title: Model router for Microsoft Foundry – Microsoft Learn
model-router.notes: Model router is a trained language model that picks a suitable large language model for each prompt in real time, and it is deployed as a single model deployment that draws on existing models. It aims to combine strong performance with lower compute cost. Three routing modes exist: Balanced, the default, which optimizes cost while keeping quality; Quality, for critical work such as legal review or complex reasoning; and Cost, for high-volume, budget-focused workloads such as classification. Administrators can limit routing to a chosen subset of models, and newly released models stay excluded until added explicitly. Models from several vendors, including OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, DeepSeek and Meta, are supported, although Claude models must be deployed separately from the model catalog. Session affinity, still in preview, tries to keep related chat requests on the same model through a session id. The response field named model shows which model answered, and metrics are available in Azure Monitor. Content filters and token rate limits apply to the router as a whole. Selection is not predictable, latency is higher than with a direct model because of routing overhead, and changes to mode or subset can take a few minutes to apply.

multi-user-authorization.title: Multi-user authorization using Resource Guard – Azure Backup – Microsoft Learn
multi-user-authorization.notes: Multi-user authorization adds a protection layer to critical operations on Recovery Services vaults and Backup vaults in Azure Backup. It relies on a separate Azure resource called a Resource Guard, which acts as an extra authorization step and may sit in a different subscription or tenant than the vault. A defined list of critical operations is covered. Disabling soft delete or security features and removing the protection itself are mandatory and cannot be excluded, while others such as stopping backup with data retention, modifying policy or disabling immutability are optional; restore is switched off by default. Duties are split between a backup admin, who owns the vault, and a security admin, who owns the Resource Guard. When the backup admin needs a critical action, the security admin temporarily grants the Backup MUA Operator role, for example through just-in-time access in Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management. The guard must be owned by someone other than the vault admin, and the vault admin needs the Reader role on it to enable the feature. If the vault admin holds Contributor, Backup MUA Admin or Backup MUA Operator on the guard, the protection is overridden. Operations performed directly on the data source fall outside the protection.

multistage-approvals.title: Multistage approvals in agent flows – Microsoft Copilot Studio – Microsoft Learn
multistage-approvals.notes: Multistage approvals support complex approval processes in Copilot Studio agent flows by combining human and AI-based review of instructions, documents and images. They build on standard approvals from cloud flows. The goal is to process routine cases automatically while people keep control over complex decisions. A flow is made of manual stages, where human approvers respond either as first to respond or with everyone required to approve, and AI stages, where a model receives instructions and inputs and returns approve or reject with a reason. Conditions placed between stages can approve, reject, redirect or skip stages based on inputs, which may be strings, numbers or booleans. The flow uses the Run a multistage approval action of the Human review connector. The feature is available only in agent flows, and AI stages need Copilot Credits assigned to the environment, otherwise the approval stalls. The page gives an expense approval as an example, combining AI screening, a manager check and a finance review. The feature is in preview and not meant for production. The same approver cannot be assigned in several stages, file attachments and application lifecycle management are not supported, and sensitive financial or legal decisions should keep human stages.

naming-convention.title: Define your naming convention – Cloud Adoption Framework – Microsoft Learn
naming-convention.notes: A naming convention sets standardized formats for naming Azure resources, aiming at clarity, consistency and compliance with Azure naming requirements. The page belongs to the Ready phase of the Cloud Adoption Framework and offers a baseline that each organization has to adapt. Typical components are a resource type abbreviation such as rg, vm or st, the workload or application, the environment such as prod or dev, the region and an instance number. Rules include a fixed order of components, an optional separator such as a hyphen and abbreviations to stay within length limits. A name is valid within a scope: global for items such as storage accounts and container registries, resource group for items such as virtual networks and virtual machines, or the parent resource for items such as subnets. The open-source Azure Naming Tool can generate names from a configured convention. Because most resource names cannot be changed after creation, only lasting information belongs in the name and other details belong in tags. Each resource type has its own limits on length and characters, not every resource allows hyphens, and personal or confidential data must stay out of names and tags. The examples are guidance rather than binding rules.

number-matching.title: How number matching works in multifactor authentication push notifications – Microsoft Learn
number-matching.notes: Number matching is a security improvement for Microsoft Authenticator push notifications. During sign-in the user sees a number and must type it into the Authenticator prompt to approve, instead of simply tapping approve or deny. It is enabled for all Authenticator push notifications, and users cannot opt out. It applies to multifactor authentication, self-service password reset with Authenticator and combined registration, plus AD FS through the adapter and NPS through a different mechanism. With same-device sign-in, users in Microsoft apps such as Teams or Outlook can choose approve or deny without typing the number, while browsers still require it; administrators do not need to configure this, but users need the current Authenticator version. Older Authenticator versions that lack number matching cannot sign in. AD FS needs specific Windows Server updates, otherwise it keeps showing approve or deny. The NPS extension asks for a one-time passcode instead and the server must use PAP, because MSCHAPv2 does not support TOTP. Push notifications on Apple Watch and Android wearables are not supported, so approval has to happen on the phone. The retired Azure Multifactor Authentication Server does not offer number matching. The page lists no license requirements.

on-behalf-of-flow.title: Microsoft identity platform and OAuth 2.0 On-Behalf-Of flow – Microsoft Learn
on-behalf-of-flow.notes: The On-Behalf-Of flow covers the case where a web API uses an identity other than its own to call another web API, which OAuth calls delegation. Its purpose is to pass the user's identity and permissions along the request chain. The client calls the middle-tier API with an access token meant for that API, and the middle tier authenticates to the token endpoint and exchanges that token for a new one aimed at the downstream API, sending it as a bearer token. A request uses the jwt-bearer grant type with the incoming token as assertion, the requested scope and requested_token_use set to on_behalf_of. The middle-tier app is a confidential client authenticating with a secret or a certificate, and consent must be arranged in advance, for example through known client applications or admin consent, because no user interaction is possible there. Only delegated scopes work, not application roles, and the flow needs a user principal, so app-only tokens cannot be used. A token issued for another resource, such as Microsoft Graph, cannot be exchanged. Tokens should not be handed on to clients, and when Conditional Access demands more, the API returns a 401 with a claims challenge. Combining the .default scope with other delegated scopes causes an error.

origin-group.title: Set up an Azure Front Door origin – Microsoft Learn
origin-group.notes: An origin group in Azure Front Door is a set of origins, meaning backends, that is attached to a route and defines how traffic reaches those origins. In the Standard and Premium tiers it corresponds to the backend pool of Azure Front Door classic, and the article applies only to those tiers. Each origin has a type, either automatically discovered for App Service, Cloud Service and Storage or a custom one for backends outside Azure. Further settings include the host name, the origin host header, certificate subject name validation for end-to-end TLS, HTTP and HTTPS ports, a priority, a weight and an enabled status. Priority separates primary, secondary and backup origins, while weight shares traffic proportionally, so an origin with twice the weight gets twice the traffic. Private Link can connect to services such as Blob Storage, static websites, App Services and internal load balancers. Health probes and load-balancing settings are set on the origin group, and session affinity can send the same user to the same origin. The portal does not check whether an origin is reachable from Front Door, so that must be verified manually. A disabled origin has routing and health probes turned off, the probe path is case sensitive, and the origin response timeout applies profile-wide.

outlook-actionable-messages.title: Actionable messages in Outlook – Microsoft Learn
outlook-actionable-messages.notes: Actionable messages let people carry out quick actions directly inside Outlook. Developers embed actions in emails or notifications, with surveys, expense approvals and CRM opportunity updates named as examples. The aim is more user interaction with services and higher productivity. A message card shows information plus action buttons such as approve and decline, then refreshes to show the result and removes the buttons once the action is complete. Supported formats are actionable messages from version 1.4 and adaptive cards up to version 1.0, while the legacy MessageCard format is not supported on Mac, iOS and Android. Authentication is token based and uses Microsoft Entra ID, and the move away from legacy authentication tokens was completed on 8 June 2026, so integrations that were not updated stop working. The feature is available for mailboxes in Exchange Online or Outlook.com with a supported client, including Outlook on the web, Microsoft 365 Apps on several update channels, and Outlook for Mac, iOS and Android. Office Professional Plus with Click-to-Run and Outlook on the web for on-premises Exchange are not supported. Known limits are missing dark mode support and no support in mobile browsers.

partner-admin-link.title: Link a partner ID to your Azure accounts (PAL) – Partner Center – Microsoft Learn
partner-admin-link.notes: A Partner Admin Link connects a partner ID to a partner's user account or service principal so that Microsoft can recognize partners who help drive Azure customer success. It applies to subscriptions on the Modern Commerce Platform. Microsoft can attribute influenced and Azure-consumed revenue based on the Azure role and scope the linked account holds, and the tracking is automated without further input from the partner. The link can be created in the Azure portal, with the Az.ManagementPartner PowerShell module or with the managementpartner Azure CLI extension, using the Associated PartnerID from the partner profile. It can later be updated or removed, and only the partner, not the customer or other partners, can change it. As a prerequisite, the customer must first give the partner access, for example as a guest user, directory account, service principal or through Azure Lighthouse, and the linked account needs an Azure RBAC role on at least one subscription or resource, or the customer will not appear in reports. The link does not change permissions or give extra service data to the partner or Microsoft. For Enterprise Agreement subscriptions the page points to a different mechanism, DPOR.

pass-through-authentication.title: Microsoft Entra pass-through authentication: How it works – Microsoft Learn
pass-through-authentication.notes: Pass-through authentication is a sign-in method in which Microsoft Entra ID hands the user name and password to on-premises Active Directory for validation, so people can sign in to Entra-based applications with their on-premises passwords. The flow involves three parts. Microsoft Entra ID receives the sign-in request, places the user name and the password, encrypted with the public key of the authentication agents, into a queue and evaluates the answer. An on-premises authentication agent retrieves requests over a persistent outbound connection, decrypts the password with its private key and validates the credentials against Active Directory using standard Windows APIs. The domain controller returns success, failure, password expired or user locked out. The user name is the userPrincipalName by default, or another attribute configured in Microsoft Entra Connect as an alternate ID. On success, Entra ID either signs the user in immediately or requires multifactor authentication. The method must be enabled in the tenant, and users must be provisioned from on-premises Active Directory through Microsoft Entra Connect, because cloud-only users are not supported. License requirements are not stated.

password-hash-synchronization.title: What is password hash synchronization with Microsoft Entra ID? – Microsoft Learn
password-hash-synchronization.notes: Password hash synchronization is one of several sign-in methods for hybrid identities. Microsoft Entra Connect synchronizes a hash of a user's password from an on-premises Active Directory instance to a cloud-based Microsoft Entra instance, extending the directory synchronization that Entra Connect Sync already performs. As a result, users manage only one password, the one in on-premises Active Directory, which the page lists as improving productivity and lowering help desk costs. Typical use is signing in to Microsoft Entra services such as Microsoft 365 with the on-premises password. It can also serve as an optional backup when AD FS is the main method. Setup consists of installing the sync agent, configuring directory synchronization between on-premises Active Directory and Microsoft Entra, and enabling password hash synchronization. The page also describes leaked credential detection for hybrid accounts: Microsoft compares publicly available username and password pairs with accounts, and a match sets the account to high risk. Only leaks discovered after PHS was enabled are compared, so pairs found earlier are not checked. License requirements and technical limits are not described on the page.

power-apps-barcode-scanner.title: Barcode scanner control in Power Apps – Microsoft Learn
power-apps-barcode-scanner.notes: The barcode scanner control in Power Apps is a legacy canvas control for scanning barcodes, QR codes and Data Matrix codes on Android, iOS and Windows devices. It is retired and replaced by the barcode reader control, which the page recommends using where possible, although existing functionality continues to be supported. The control is a button that opens the native scanner on the device and detects codes automatically once they are in view; it does not display the result itself, and scanning in a web browser is not supported. Output is available through Value, the text of the last scanned code, and Type, the code type. OnScan fires after a successful scan and OnCancel when the user cancels. Configuration options include BarcodeType, which defaults to Auto and can combine several types, PreferFrontCamera and FlashlightEnabled. To use it, the app must be opened in edit mode and the Legacy barcode scanner option enabled under Settings, Upcoming features, Retired. For accessibility, the scanned value can be shown in a label whose Live property is set to Polite, and an alternative input such as a text box should be offered. Supported code types vary by platform, and some formats are unavailable on Windows or not supported at all.

power-apps-component-library.title: Component library application lifecycle management – Power Apps – Microsoft Learn
power-apps-component-library.notes: A component library is a special type of canvas app that holds one or more canvas components. Unlike app-level components, which are limited to a single app, library components can be used by every other canvas app in the same environment. A component must first be imported into an app, which copies its definition into that app, so the app becomes self-contained for that definition. Updates to the library are offered in the consuming app through a notice when the app is opened for editing or on request, and changes should be made in the library itself so the connection is kept. A library can be included in a Dataverse solution; in an environment with Dataverse it lands automatically in the default solution. The managed property Allow customizations decides whether the library can be edited in the target environment. Apps that use library components are marked as dependent, so importing a solution without the library fails with a missing dependency message, and even an imported but unused component creates a dependency. Application lifecycle features need a Dataverse environment, and the page names no license requirements. A solution export always contains the newest library version.

power-apps-containers.title: Build responsive layouts in canvas apps – Power Apps – Microsoft Learn
power-apps-containers.notes: Containers are described as the building blocks of responsive design in canvas apps. A container is either an auto layout container, which can be vertical or horizontal, or a fixed layout container, for which constraint support is only planned. UI elements are placed inside a container, and the container's own responsive properties decide how it positions and scales on different screen sizes and how its children are arranged. In an auto layout container the position of children is set automatically, so X and Y do not need to be entered. Available properties include alignment, justification, fill portions, flexible width and height, gap, wrap and overflow, with overflow values such as stretch, start, end, center, space between and scroll. To build responsive screens, the display settings Scale to fit, Lock aspect ratio and Lock orientation must be turned off. The new layouts are available for app formats generally, while the new screen templates exist only for tablet format. Typical uses are screens that react to size or form factor changes, stacking elements horizontally or vertically and spacing them evenly. Known issues include ignored alignment when wrap is on and no support for data tables or charts inside layout containers.

power-apps-delegation.title: Understand delegation in a canvas app – Power Apps – Microsoft Learn
power-apps-delegation.notes: Delegation means that Power Apps passes a Power Fx query on to the data source as an equivalent query, so the source runs it and returns only the results. A query is nondelegable when it uses a feature the data source does not support, and if any part of an expression is nondelegable, none of the query is delegated. Data sources named as delegable include Dataverse, SharePoint, SQL Server and Salesforce, while imported Excel workbooks, collections and tables in context variables already live in memory. Functions such as Filter, Search, First, LookUp, Sort and SortByColumns can be delegated, together with logical and comparison operators, StartsWith, EndsWith, IsBlank and, depending on backend support, aggregates such as Sum, Average and CountRows. Functions such as If, Mid, Len, Lower, Upper, Text, Value, FirstN, Last and GroupBy cannot be delegated. When a formula is not delegable, it is processed locally on a limited number of records, 500 by default, adjustable through the data row limit setting up to a maximum. Records beyond the limit are missed, so a Filter can fail to find them and Average covers only those records. The editor warns about nondelegable expressions, but only for delegable data sources.

power-apps-vibe.title: Power Apps vibe experience overview – Microsoft Learn
power-apps-vibe.notes: The Power Apps vibe experience is described as an AI-native platform that creates solutions for business problems, covering requirements, data and complete apps with generated code. A description in natural language produces a data model, business logic and user interface, and planning, data modeling and app building happen in one workspace, with changes carried across all components. At the prompt, users can use plan mode to review and discuss a plan with the agent before changes are made, optionally enhance the prompt, dictate by voice or pick suggested examples. The page names business analysts, citizen developers and professional developers as the audience, with onboarding apps, inventory management, project tracking and departmental workflows as examples. A tenant administrator must enable Copilot in Power Apps preview in the Power Platform admin center, and enabling external models is optional but recommended for higher app quality. It is not available in the default environment, is limited to certain regions and works only in English. The experience is a preview, not intended for production use, and the page notes that app creation is now available in Copilot Cowork and is being rolled out to Microsoft Copilot Studio, which Microsoft recommends for the future.

power-automate-concurrency-control.title: Implement parallel execution – Power Automate – Microsoft Learn
power-automate-concurrency-control.notes: Parallel execution means a flow runs two or more steps at the same time, and the workflow continues only after all parallel steps have finished. Concurrency control applies to the Apply to each loop, whose items are processed one after another by default but can be handled simultaneously through the degree of parallelism setting, which the maker chooses within a range from 1 to 50. The aim is more efficient processing and shorter run time, especially for asynchronous tasks. The page suggests parallelism for independent tasks that take longer than about five seconds. Typical uses include approvals that must not block other actions, quorum-based approvals, creating or updating records in several systems at once, retrieving data from several sources and merging it, sending individual emails to many recipients and creating many users in Microsoft Entra ID. There are limits: splitting work, thread queues and delays of the called endpoint add overhead, so a very high value does not always help. Skipped actions confuse the flow logic and still use resources, so child flows are advised instead. The setting works only at the top level of the cloud flow, and nested Apply to each actions always run sequentially. No license requirements are given.
